narrative: Material PL3__M05EDAA4 displays smooth, high-volume daily demand (mean ~590 units, CV=0.061) that is approximately normally distributed with no detectable trend. Lead times are volatile (CV=0.806, range 0.5–3.73 days), making lead-time variability the dominant driver of safety stock. A continuous-review (r,Q) reorder point policy is recommended: reorder at 1,547 units and place orders of 1,733 units, maintaining 883 units safety stock to achieve the 95% service level. The EOQ was capacity-constrained from 3,721 to 1,733 units to respect the 2,616-unit storage limit.
warnings: Order quantity reduced from 3721 to 1733 due to max_storage_units capacity constraint (883 + 1733 = 2616 <= 2616.196)

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth and approximately normal demand (CV=0.061) with volatile lead times (CV=0.806) is the ideal profile for a fixed (r,Q) policy. The reorder point absorbs lead-time uncertainty via a statistically calibrated safety stock, while EOQ minimises total ordering and holding cost without requiring periodic review overhead.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (2,616 units) caps the order quantity at 1,733 units, nearly doubling the ordering frequency vs. the unconstrained EOQ of 3,721 units. This adds approximately $4,700/year in ordering cost. Expanding storage by ~1,100 units would unlock full EOQ savings.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (411) + safety_stock (883) = 1,294 which is below max_storage_units (2,616). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
